newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes slightly firmer, remains quiet.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes slightly firmer, remains quiet.

text.p: Precious metals prices were mildly firmer from their earlier levels on Wednesday afternoon reflecting New York's in-line opening.
Dealers noted earlier that a late New York rally in gold on Tuesday failed to follow through into Far East trading leading Europe to open mildly bearish especially in silver.
"London and Europe is bearish for gold and silver but New York seems to have a much more bullish view," one dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $351.05 per ounce against $350.70 on Wednesday morning and $350.00 on Tuesday afternoon.
Business was fairly light although gold had received some support from the sharp falls in the U.S. equities markets this week.
"The interest from people coming out of equities has been fairly minor. It is not yet clear whether or not this is the beginning of a collapse (in equities) or a correction," one dealer said.
The market was wary of the strength of the U.S. economy and steadiness of the dollar, dealers said.
Last week's 25-basis point rise in the U.S. Fed Funds rate was well anticipated and caused no more than a 50-cent ripple in gold prices.
However the possibility of a rise in the discount rate meant the market remained cautious.

Dealers said the bias today would be towards the downside, at least until the opening in New York where the mood was a little "There is a chance we will see a break towards $348.00," one dealer said, although others emphasised that the price had little incentive to move much from the $350.00 level.
The white metals were suffering more than gold from the higher U.S. interest rates and possibility of further economy-dampening moves, dealers said.
Silver struggled to get back over $5.00 aided by a steady start on Comex having opened seven cents down at $4.96/$4.98.
By 1415 GMT it was indicated at $5.02/$5.04, around its highest of the European trading day.
Platinum and palladium were also firmer at $371.00/$372.00, up $2.00 on the Tuesday close and $149.75/$150.75, $3.00 ahead respectively.
Dealers said there was still no sign of a conclusion to the impasse which had halted exports of Russian platinum group metals to Japan since last November.
